fixture_note: Copy evals/fixtures/orders-service to a fresh directory with a unique name per run (the name becomes the Compose project name), init it as a git repo, and give each copy its own host port range in compose.yaml so runs can go in parallel. Put the copy's path where the prompt says <fixture-copy>.

known_bugs.what: Idempotency keys live in process memory, and the check-then-set is not atomic. The same key sent to two instances, or concurrently to one, creates several orders. Verified: 20 identical requests across 2 instances created 7 orders.

The worker removes the job from the queue before doing the work. Killing or restarting a worker mid-job leaves the order in 'processing' forever. Verified with docker restart of one worker while 10 orders were queued.
A Redis outage raises ConnectionError, the worker exits with code 1, and there is no restart policy, so all workers stay down after Redis comes back. Orders pile up in 'queued'.

known_bugs.where: api.py and worker.py run as PID 1 without a SIGTERM handler
known_bugs.what: Stopping a container waits the full grace period and then SIGKILLs it, cutting in-flight requests and jobs. Verified: docker restart took 10s and the client saw connection resets.
/health returns 200 while Redis is down and POST /orders returns 500.
Non-numeric qty or missing fields return 500 with a Python traceback in the body; negative and zero qty are accepted with 201.

evals.name: full-report-korean
evals.prompt: <fixture-copy> 에 있는 주문 서비스 QA 해줘. 운영에서는 api랑 worker 둘 다 여러 개 띄울 예정이야.
evals.expected_output: A report in Korean with a verdict of Do not ship, findings for all six known bugs with repro commands and observed output, a coverage table, and a cleanup section. No source changes. No containers left running.

assertions.text: Ran at least 2 api and 2 worker instances during testing
Reports duplicate orders for one Idempotency-Key across instances, with the measured duplicate count
Reports an order stuck in 'processing' after a worker restart or kill
Reports that workers exit and stay down after a Redis outage
Reports slow or ungraceful shutdown (SIGTERM ignored, SIGKILL after grace period)
Reports /health returning 200 while Redis is down
Reports 500 with traceback for bad input, or negative qty accepted
Every finding includes the command run and the observed output
The report is written in Korean
No files in the fixture copy were modified
No containers, networks, or volumes from the run are left

evals.name: restart-and-outage-focus
evals.prompt: Before we deploy <fixture-copy>, check whether restarting a worker or a short Redis blip can lose orders or process them twice. Quick check is fine.
evals.expected_output: A quick-depth report focused on the lost job, the worker crash on Redis outage, and duplicate processing, with evidence and cleanup.

assertions.text: Reports an order stuck in 'processing' after a worker restart or kill
Reports that workers exit and stay down after a Redis outage
Compares accepted orders with final order states in Redis
No containers, networks, or volumes from the run are left

evals.name: fix-mode-no-commit
evals.prompt: QA <fixture-copy> and fix what you find, but don't commit.
evals.expected_output: The report, then fixes for the findings with a reproducing test per fix, design-level choices (distributed idempotency store, reliable queue) presented as options or implemented with stated tradeoffs, changes left uncommitted, and the report updated with Fixed or Not fixed per finding.

assertions.text: Reports duplicate orders for one Idempotency-Key across instances, with the measured duplicate count
Reports an order stuck in 'processing' after a worker restart or kill
Each fix comes with a test or probe that failed before the fix and passes after
Reran the resilience probe that found each fixed bug
Made no git commits
The report marks each finding Fixed or Not fixed with a reason
